Wireland / Design reference

One visual language.
Every experience.

Shared foundations and component examples for the website, Patient, Doctor, and Admin dashboards. This is the starting reference; additional variants and interactions will be documented as they are defined.

Colors

Choose colors by purpose: backgrounds, text, actions, and messages. Pair status colors with clear text so meaning does not depend on color alone.

Source: assets/css/app.css

Font Size

Choose a size that matches the role of the text. Title sizes adapt from mobile to desktop, while body and supporting text keep a consistent size.

Source: assets/css/app.css

Type Scale

Each size utility includes its line-height. Keep font weight separate and avoid leading-* overrides unless a control needs specific alignment. Body text uses text-base or inherits 16px; there is no text-body token.

Title / Large

36px / 60px · Line-height 1.1

Hero and single-page titles.

text-title-lg font-medium

Care starts here.

Title / Medium

28px / 36px · Line-height 1.25

Section headings and consultation banners. The default headline variant uses this token.

text-title-md font-medium

Care that fits your life.

Title / Small

20px / 24px · Line-height 1.3

Subheadings, testimonial quotes, assessment titles, and step headings.

text-title-sm font-medium

Your next chapter starts here.

Body / Default

16px / 16px · Line-height 1.5

Reading content and compact titles. Inherit 16px where the parent already provides it; use text-base when an explicit size is needed.

text-base font-normal

Find the information you need in one place.

Small

14px / 14px · Line-height 1.5

Supporting descriptions, navigation, field labels, and compact interface text.

text-small font-normal

Additional information about your account.

Caption

12px / 12px · Line-height 1.5

Metadata, badges, helper text, and short supporting notes.

text-caption font-normal

Additional product details.

Font Weight

Choose font weight independently of size. Use regular for reading, medium for labels and headings, and heavier weights for deliberate emphasis.

Source: assets/css/app.css

Weight Scale

Use regular (400) for reading and input values, and medium (500) for labels, buttons, and metrics. Use semibold (600) for section headings or selected emphasis, and bold (700) for deliberate emphasis. Font weight stays independent of size and does not change automatically by viewport.

Input

Use inputs for short, single-line values such as names, email addresses, and passwords. Keep filled, read-only, disabled, and error states easy to distinguish.

Source: views/components/forms/field.php

Input Group

A text input and action button inside one field outline. The action uses the shared small button (32px). Place the component inside a form to submit its value.

Source: views/components/forms/input-group.php

Input Group Text

Keep currency, units or reference values visible before or after an input. The surrounding text cannot be edited.

Source: views/components/forms/input-group.php

RM
RM
kg
RM RM 150.00

Set before for a prefix, after for a suffix, or both for combined. Only the input value is submitted; text stays visible while typing. Use short affixes.

Textarea

Use textareas for longer responses. They grow with their content and shrink back to the minimum height set by rows (default: 3 lines), including the control padding and border. Browsers without native field sizing use the configured row count and manual resizing.

Source: views/components/forms/field.php

Checkbox Layouts

Vertical
Horizontal

Rows have a 24px minimum height and grow with wrapped labels. Vertical groups use an 8px gap. Horizontal groups use a 24px column gap and a 12px row gap, wrapping onto the next line. These examples demonstrate selection only; they do not change account settings.

Vertical: flex flex-col items-start gap-2
Horizontal: flex flex-wrap items-start gap-x-6 gap-y-3
Group label: mb-3. Between groups: gap-8. See docs/forms.md for usage and keyboard guidance.

File Upload

Local selection, previews, removal and ordering. The consuming page handles saving or uploading.

Up to 4 images · JPEG, PNG or WebP · 1 MB each.

0/4 files selected

      No files selected. Drop files here or choose below.

      Drop files in this panel. Drag selected files to reorder, or use the arrow buttons.

      Up to 2 documents · PDF or TXT · 5 MB each.

      0/2 files selected

          No files selected. Drop files here or choose below.

          Drop files in this panel. Drag selected files to reorder, or use the arrow buttons.

          Use component('forms/file-upload', $config) with a unique id, name, label, accept, max_files and max_size in bytes.

          Load assets/js/file-upload.js once. Use FileUpload.init(root) to access getFiles() for FormData, getItems() for ordered files and existing URLs, setValues(urls) for existing images, and isBusy(). Listen for file-upload:change.

          Image Choices

          Use image choices when illustrations help explain the options. Pair each image with a clear label and allow one selection per group.

          Source: views/components/forms/choice.php

          Selected

          Toggle Collapse

          Show or hide a content group with an optional count.

          Source: views/components/toggle-collapse.php

          This group starts expanded. Select the heading to hide its content.

          This group starts collapsed and has no count.

          Use component('toggle-collapse', $config) with label and controls matching a unique panel ID. Optional: count_label and expanded (default true). Use variant: plain (default) or variant: filled for a background and horizontal padding.

          Default spacing between collapse groups: grid gap-5 on the parent. Keep headings free of margins. Put mt-3 or pt-3 on the controlled panel so its spacing disappears when hidden. Keep any other content spacing inside that panel.

          Full usage and spacing guidance: docs/toggle-collapse.md.

          For expanded: false, add hidden to the panel. Load assets/js/toggle-collapse.js once. Tab focuses the button; Enter or Space toggles the panel.

          Tabs

          Use tabs to switch between related panels. Underline is the default; Segmented is an optional variant. Choose default (14px, 40px tall) or small (12px, 32px tall). Tabs stay on one horizontally scrolling row. Use arrow keys, Home, and End to move between tabs.

          Modal

          Use a centered modal for a short review or decision. One size, with a maximum width of 32rem. Close with the close button, Cancel, Escape, or the backdrop. Focus returns to the opening control. Longer content scrolls while the header and optional footer stay visible. Open one dialog at a time.

          Source: views/components/modal.php · assets/js/modal.js

          Review before continuing

          Check the details before taking the next step.

          Use this space for a short summary or a decision. Both actions close this demonstration; no data is submitted.

          Drawer

          Use a right-side drawer for a short preview while keeping the current page in place. The header and optional footer stay visible while longer content scrolls. Close with the close button, Escape, or the backdrop. Focus returns to the opening control.

          Source: views/components/drawer.php · assets/js/drawer.js

          Preview

          A brief summary before opening the full record.

          Dropdown

          Use dropdowns for actions and links. Open below or above the trigger, with automatic fallback when space is limited. Use arrow keys, Home and End to navigate; Escape closes the menu and returns focus. Use Select for form values. Demo actions only report your selection; they do not change records.

          Source: views/components/dropdown.php · assets/js/overlays.js
